System.out.println("row " + i + " differs from D at " + i + ": " + ___);
explanation: Every row differs from D at its own index, so D is not any row. In the real argument the table is infinite — rows are all programs, which are countable — and D is `trouble`. The finite table is the picture, not the proof: the proof needs the rows to be *all* programs, which is what the countability argument supplies.
